title: 03. Embeddings & Vector DBs: Complete RAG Indexing Techniques — Master Guide 2026
summary: Core Idea: Convert documents → vectors → store in index → when query comes, find nearest vectors → feed to LLM

sections.title: FOUNDATION — What is RAG Indexing?
sections.body:
```
RAG Pipeline:
┌─────────────┐    ┌──────────────┐    ┌─────────────┐    ┌──────────┐
│  Documents  │───▶│  Embeddings  │───▶│    INDEX    │───▶│   LLM   │
│  (Raw Text) │    │  (Vectors)   │    │  (Storage)  │    │(Answer) │
└─────────────┘    └──────────────┘    └─────────────┘    └──────────┘
                                              ▲
                                        Query Vector
                                        searches here
```

> **Core Idea:** Convert documents → vectors → store in index → when query comes, find nearest vectors → feed to LLM

sections.title: Concept Explanation
sections.body:
```
FLAT INDEX = Compare your query against EVERY SINGLE vector in the database
             No shortcuts. No approximations. Pure math.

Formula: similarity(q, d) = cosine(q, d) OR euclidean_distance(q, d)

✅ 100% Accurate (exact nearest neighbor)
❌ Slow at scale (O(n) per query)
✅ Best when: dataset < 100K vectors
```

sections.title: Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
FLAT INDEX — How it works:

Query Vector Q = [0.2, 0.8, 0.5]

Database:
Vector 1: [0.1, 0.9, 0.4]  ──▶ distance = 0.12  ← Closest!
Vector 2: [0.9, 0.1, 0.2]  ──▶ distance = 0.87
Vector 3: [0.3, 0.7, 0.6]  ──▶ distance = 0.18
Vector 4: [0.8, 0.2, 0.1]  ──▶ distance = 0.92
Vector 5: [0.2, 0.8, 0.4]  ──▶ distance = 0.11  ← 2nd closest!
         ...calculate ALL...
Vector N: [0.5, 0.5, 0.5]  ──▶ distance = 0.45

Result: Sort all distances → Return top-K

⚡ Speed vs Accuracy:
  Accuracy: ████████████████████ 100%
  Speed:    ████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░  20% (slow for large data)
```

sections.title: CODE EXAMPLE 1 — FAISS Flat Index (Basic RAG)
sections.body:
```python
# pip install faiss-cpu==1.9.0 sentence-transformers==3.4.0 numpy==2.2.0

import faiss
import numpy as np
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer

# ── Step 1: Load latest embedding model ──────────────────────────────
model = SentenceTransformer("sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2")  # 2026 latest

# ── Step 2: Sample document corpus ───────────────────────────────────
documents = [
    "Python is a high-level programming language known for simplicity.",
    "Machine learning uses algorithms to learn from data.",
    "RAG combines retrieval systems with language models.",
    "Flat indexing checks every vector for similarity.",
    "Neural networks are the backbone of deep learning.",
    "Vector databases store high-dimensional embeddings efficiently.",
    "FAISS is Facebook's library for similarity search.",
    "Transformers revolutionized natural language processing in 2017.",
]

# ── Step 3: Generate embeddings ───────────────────────────────────────
print("🔄 Generating embeddings...")
embeddings = model.encode(documents, normalize_embeddings=True)
# Shape: (8, 384) — 8 docs, 384 dimensions

dimension = embeddings.shape[1]  # 384
print(f"✅ Embedding shape: {embeddings.shape}")

# ── Step 4: Build FLAT INDEX (IndexFlatIP = Inner Product = Cosine) ───
index = faiss.IndexFlatIP(dimension)  # IP = Inner Product (cosine when normalized)

# Add vectors to index
index.add(embeddings.astype(np.float32))
print(f"✅ Index built with {index.ntotal} vectors")

# ── Step 5: Query the index ────────────────────────────────────────────
query = "How does retrieval augmented generation work?"
query_embedding = model.encode([query], normalize_embeddings=True)

# Search: k=3 means return top 3 results
distances, indices = index.search(query_embedding.astype(np.float32), k=3)

# ── Step 6: Display results ────────────────────────────────────────────
print(f"\n🔍 Query: {query}")
print("=" * 60)
print("📌 Top-3 Retrieved Documents (Flat/Exact Search):")
for rank, (dist, idx) in enumerate(zip(distances[0], indices[0])):
    print(f"\nRank {rank+1}:")
    print(f"  📄 Document: {documents[idx]}")
    print(f"  📊 Similarity Score: {dist:.4f}")

# Output:
# Rank 1: "RAG combines retrieval systems with language models."  Score: 0.7823
# Rank 2: "Vector databases store high-dimensional embeddings."   Score: 0.6541
# Rank 3: "Flat indexing checks every vector for similarity."     Score: 0.5932
```

sections.body:
```python
# pip install chromadb==0.6.3 sentence-transformers==3.4.0

import chromadb
from chromadb.utils import embedding_functions
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer

# ── ChromaDB uses Flat Index by default (HNSW optional) ──────────────

# Step 1: Initialize ChromaDB client (in-memory for demo)
client = chromadb.Client()

# Step 2: Custom embedding function with latest model
embedding_fn = embedding_functions.SentenceTransformerEmbeddingFunction(
    model_name="sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2"  # 2026 latest
)

# Step 3: Create collection (Flat index under the hood)
collection = client.create_collection(
    name="medical_knowledge_base",
    embedding_function=embedding_fn,
    metadata={"hnsw:space": "cosine"}  # distance metric
)

# Step 4: Add medical documents
medical_docs = [
    "Diabetes is a chronic condition affecting blood sugar regulation.",
    "Hypertension is elevated blood pressure above 140/90 mmHg.",
    "Antibiotics treat bacterial infections but not viral ones.",
    "The heart pumps blood through the circulatory system.",
    "Insulin is a hormone produced by the pancreas.",
    "COVID-19 is caused by the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus.",
    "Vaccines stimulate the immune system to fight diseases.",
    "MRI scans use magnetic fields to create detailed body images.",
]

collection.add(
    documents=medical_docs,
    ids=[f"doc_{i}" for i in range(len(medical_docs))],
    metadatas=[{"category": "medicine", "doc_id": i} for i in range(len(medical_docs))]
)

print(f"✅ Collection has {collection.count()} documents")

# Step 5: Query
results = collection.query(
    query_texts=["What causes high blood sugar in diabetic patients?"],
    n_results=3,
    include=["documents", "distances", "metadatas"]
)

print("\n🔍 Query: What causes high blood sugar in diabetic patients?")
print("=" * 65)
for i, (doc, dist) in enumerate(zip(
    results['documents'][0],
    results['distances'][0]
)):
    print(f"\nRank {i+1}:")
    print(f"  📄 {doc}")
    print(f"  📊 Distance: {dist:.4f}")
```

sections.title: Concept Explanation
sections.body:
```
HNSW = A GRAPH-based index structure with MULTIPLE LAYERS
       Like a highway system — express lanes for fast travel,
       local roads for precision

Key Parameters:
  M        = Number of connections per node (default: 16)
             Higher M = Better recall, More memory
  ef_construction = Search width during BUILD (default: 200)
  ef_search = Search width during QUERY (higher = more accurate)

✅ Near-perfect accuracy (ANN — Approximate Nearest Neighbor)
✅ Very fast query time O(log n)
✅ Best for: 100K to 100M vectors
❌ High memory usage
❌ Slow index build time
```

sections.title: Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
HNSW STRUCTURE — Multi-Layer Graph:

Layer 2 (Express Highway — fewest nodes):
    A ──────────────── E

Layer 1 (Regional Roads — more nodes):
    A ──── B ──── C ──── D ──── E

Layer 0 (Local Streets — ALL nodes):
    A─B─C─D─E─F─G─H─I─J─K─L─M─N─O─P

SEARCH PROCESS for Query Q:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. START at top layer (Layer 2) — few nodes         │
│    Navigate greedily to closest node                │
│                                                     │
│ 2. DROP DOWN to Layer 1                             │
│    Continue greedy navigation from entry point      │
│                                                     │
│ 3. DROP DOWN to Layer 0 (bottom)                    │
│    Fine-grained search among neighbors              │
│                                                     │
│ 4. RETURN top-K nearest neighbors                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Speed vs Flat:
FLAT:  ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓  (check ALL)    slow
HNSW:  ▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░  (skip most)   FAST!

⚡ HNSW Performance:
  Accuracy: ██████████████████░░ ~98%
  Speed:    ████████████████████ ~95%
```

sections.title: CODE EXAMPLE 1 — HNSW with FAISS
sections.body:
```python
# pip install faiss-cpu==1.9.0 sentence-transformers==3.4.0 numpy==2.2.0

import faiss
import numpy as np
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
import time

model = SentenceTransformer("sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2")

# ── Large corpus simulation ───────────────────────────────────────────
base_docs = [
    "Artificial intelligence is transforming healthcare diagnosis",
    "Machine learning models require large amounts of training data",
    "Natural language processing enables computers to understand text",
    "Computer vision systems can identify objects in images",
    "Reinforcement learning trains agents through reward signals",
    "Deep learning uses multiple neural network layers",
    "Transfer learning reuses pretrained model knowledge",
    "Federated learning trains models across distributed devices",
    "Attention mechanisms help models focus on relevant information",
    "Large language models can generate human-like text",
]

# Simulate 10,000 documents
documents = base_docs * 1000  # 10,000 docs
print(f"📚 Total documents: {len(documents)}")

# Generate embeddings
print("🔄 Encoding documents...")
embeddings = model.encode(documents, batch_size=256,
                           normalize_embeddings=True,
                           show_progress_bar=True)

dimension = embeddings.shape[1]  # 384
embeddings = embeddings.astype(np.float32)

# ── Build FLAT index for comparison ──────────────────────────────────
flat_index = faiss.IndexFlatIP(dimension)
t1 = time.time()
flat_index.add(embeddings)
flat_build_time = time.time() - t1
print(f"\n✅ Flat Index built in {flat_build_time:.3f}s | Vectors: {flat_index.ntotal}")

# ── Build HNSW index ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# M=32: each node connects to 32 neighbors (higher = better recall)
hnsw_index = faiss.IndexHNSWFlat(dimension, 32)  # 32 = M parameter
hnsw_index.hnsw.efConstruction = 200  # Build-time search width (higher = better index quality)

t2 = time.time()
hnsw_index.add(embeddings)
hnsw_build_time = time.time() - t2
print(f"✅ HNSW Index built in {hnsw_build_time:.3f}s | Vectors: {hnsw_index.ntotal}")

# ── Query comparison ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
query = "How do neural networks learn from examples?"
q_vec = model.encode([query], normalize_embeddings=True).astype(np.float32)

# HNSW search width (higher = more accurate but slower)
hnsw_index.hnsw.efSearch = 64

# Flat search
t3 = time.time()
flat_dist, flat_idx = flat_index.search(q_vec, k=5)
flat_query_time = (time.time() - t3) * 1000

# HNSW search
t4 = time.time()
hnsw_dist, hnsw_idx = hnsw_index.search(q_vec, k=5)
hnsw_query_time = (time.time() - t4) * 1000

print(f"\n🔍 Query: {query}")
print("=" * 65)
print(f"\n📊 PERFORMANCE COMPARISON:")
print(f"  {'Method':<15} {'Query Time':<15} {'Build Time':<15}")
print(f"  {'─'*15} {'─'*15} {'─'*15}")
print(f"  {'FLAT':<15} {flat_query_time:.2f}ms{'':<9} {flat_build_time:.3f}s")
print(f"  {'HNSW':<15} {hnsw_query_time:.2f}ms{'':<9} {hnsw_build_time:.3f}s")

print(f"\n📌 HNSW Top-5 Results:")
for rank, (dist, idx) in enumerate(zip(hnsw_dist[0], hnsw_idx[0])):
    print(f"  Rank {rank+1}: [{idx % 10}] {base_docs[idx % 10][:60]}...")
    print(f"           Score: {dist:.4f}")
```

sections.title: CODE EXAMPLE 2 — HNSW with hnswlib (Pure Python)
sections.body:
```python
# pip install hnswlib==0.8.0 sentence-transformers==3.4.0 numpy==2.2.0

import hnswlib
import numpy as np
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
import pickle

model = SentenceTransformer("sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2")

# ── E-commerce product search use case ───────────────────────────────
products = [
    {"id": 0, "name": "Apple iPhone 16 Pro Max", "desc": "Latest Apple smartphone with A18 chip"},
    {"id": 1, "name": "Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra", "desc": "Android flagship with 200MP camera"},
    {"id": 2, "name": "Sony WH-1000XM6", "desc": "Premium noise-cancelling wireless headphones"},
    {"id": 3, "name": "MacBook Pro M4", "desc": "Apple laptop with M4 chip for professionals"},
    {"id": 4, "name": "Dell XPS 15 2026", "desc": "Windows laptop with OLED display"},
    {"id": 5, "name": "iPad Pro M4", "desc": "Apple tablet with OLED display"},
    {"id": 6, "name": "AirPods Pro 3", "desc": "Wireless earbuds with active noise cancellation"},
    {"id": 7, "name": "Google Pixel 9 Pro", "desc": "Google's flagship phone with AI features"},
    {"id": 8, "name": "Nintendo Switch 2", "desc": "Handheld gaming console by Nintendo"},
    {"id": 9, "name": "PlayStation 5 Pro", "desc": "Sony's gaming console with 8K support"},
]

# Create searchable text (name + description)
texts = [f"{p['name']} - {p['desc']}" for p in products]
embeddings = model.encode(texts, normalize_embeddings=True).astype(np.float32)

dimension = embeddings.shape[1]  # 768 for mpnet
num_elements = len(products)

# ── Initialize HNSW index ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# space: 'cosine', 'l2', or 'ip' (inner product)
hnsw = hnswlib.Index(space='cosine', dim=dimension)

# init_index: max_elements, ef_construction, M
hnsw.init_index(
    max_elements=10000,    # Max capacity
    ef_construction=200,   # Build quality (higher = better graph)
    M=32                   # Connections per node
)

# Set search quality (ef >= k for query)
hnsw.set_ef(50)  # Must be >= k (number of results)

# Add items with their IDs
hnsw.add_items(embeddings, ids=list(range(num_elements)))

print(f"✅ HNSW index built | Elements: {hnsw.get_current_count()}")
print(f"   M={32}, ef_construction=200, ef_search=50")

# ── Query Examples ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
queries = [
    "best phone with great camera",
    "laptop for software developers",
    "gaming console for home entertainment",
]

for query in queries:
    q_vec = model.encode([query], normalize_embeddings=True).astype(np.float32)

    # search returns (labels, distances)
    labels, distances = hnsw.knn_query(q_vec, k=3)

    print(f"\n🔍 Query: '{query}'")
    print("─" * 55)
    for rank, (label, dist) in enumerate(zip(labels[0], distances[0])):
        product = products[label]
        similarity = 1 - dist  # cosine: distance → similarity
        print(f"  Rank {rank+1}: {product['name']}")
        print(f"           Similarity: {similarity:.4f}")

# ── Save and reload index ─────────────────────────────────────────────
hnsw.save_index("product_hnsw.bin")
print("\n💾 Index saved to product_hnsw.bin")

# Reload
hnsw_loaded = hnswlib.Index(space='cosine', dim=dimension)
hnsw_loaded.load_index("product_hnsw.bin", max_elements=10000)
print(f"✅ Index reloaded | Elements: {hnsw_loaded.get_current_count()}")
```

sections.title: Concept Explanation
sections.body:
```
IVF = Divide vectors into CLUSTERS (using K-means)
      At query time, search ONLY the nearest clusters — not everything

Key Parameters:
  nlist  = Number of clusters (cells) to create
           Rule of thumb: nlist = sqrt(N)  where N = total vectors
  nprobe = How many clusters to search at query time
           Higher nprobe = More accurate but slower
           nprobe=1 = fastest but least accurate
           nprobe=nlist = same as flat search (exact)

✅ Excellent for 100K to 10M vectors
✅ Much faster than flat (searches only subset of data)
❌ Approximate (may miss some true neighbors)
❌ Needs training phase (cluster creation)
```

sections.title: Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
IVF STRUCTURE:

BUILD PHASE (K-means clustering):
All vectors → K-means → 4 clusters (nlist=4)

     Cluster 1          Cluster 2
     ┌─────────┐        ┌─────────┐
     │ ● ● ●  │        │ ○ ○    │
     │   ●    │        │   ○ ○  │
     └─────────┘        └─────────┘
     Centroid C1        Centroid C2

     Cluster 3          Cluster 4
     ┌─────────┐        ┌─────────┐
     │ ■ ■    │        │ ▲ ▲ ▲  │
     │   ■ ■  │        │   ▲    │
     └─────────┘        └─────────┘
     Centroid C3        Centroid C4

QUERY PHASE (nprobe=2):
Query Q → Find 2 nearest centroids (C1, C3) → Search ONLY those clusters

FLAT:  Searches ALL 4 clusters = slow ✗
IVF:   Searches 2/4 clusters = 2x faster ✓

Accuracy vs Speed tradeoff (nprobe):
nprobe=1:  ████░░░░░░ 40% recall  | ██████████ 100% speed
nprobe=5:  ███████░░░ 70% recall  | ████████░░  80% speed
nprobe=20: █████████░ 90% recall  | ██████░░░░  60% speed
nprobe=nlist: ██████████ 100%     | ████░░░░░░  40% speed
```

sections.title: CODE EXAMPLE 1 — IVF with FAISS (News Article Search)
sections.body:
```python
# pip install faiss-cpu==1.9.0 sentence-transformers==3.4.0 numpy==2.2.0

import faiss
import numpy as np
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
import time

model = SentenceTransformer("sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2")

# ── News article corpus ───────────────────────────────────────────────
news_templates = [
    "The stock market reached record highs today as tech stocks surged",
    "Scientists discovered a new species of deep-sea creature in Pacific",
    "The government announced new climate change policies for 2026",
    "A major earthquake struck the coastal region causing widespread damage",
    "The football team won the championship after a dramatic final match",
    "New AI model outperforms humans in complex reasoning tasks",
    "Electric vehicle sales hit record numbers across global markets",
    "Medical researchers found breakthrough treatment for Alzheimer's disease",
    "Cryptocurrency markets experienced high volatility this week",
    "Space agency announced plans for Mars colony mission in 2030",
]

# Create 50,000 document corpus
documents = news_templates * 5000  # 50,000 docs
print(f"📚 Corpus size: {len(documents):,} documents")

# Encode in batches
print("🔄 Encoding corpus (this may take a moment)...")
embeddings = model.encode(
    documents,
    batch_size=512,
    normalize_embeddings=True,
    show_progress_bar=True
).astype(np.float32)

dimension = embeddings.shape[1]  # 384
N = len(documents)

# ── IVF Configuration ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
nlist = int(np.sqrt(N))  # Rule of thumb: sqrt(N) = ~224 clusters
print(f"\n⚙️  IVF Config: nlist={nlist}, N={N:,}")

# ── Build IVF Index ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# IndexIVFFlat = IVF with exact distance computation in each cell
quantizer = faiss.IndexFlatIP(dimension)  # Quantizer = finds nearest centroid
ivf_index = faiss.IndexIVFFlat(
    quantizer,    # Coarse quantizer
    dimension,    # Vector dimension
    nlist,        # Number of clusters
    faiss.METRIC_INNER_PRODUCT  # Use cosine (since normalized)
)

# MUST train IVF index (K-means clustering)
print(f"\n🏋️  Training IVF index (K-means with {nlist} clusters)...")
t_train = time.time()
ivf_index.train(embeddings)  # Train on data
train_time = time.time() - t_train
print(f"✅ Training completed in {train_time:.2f}s")

# Add vectors
t_add = time.time()
ivf_index.add(embeddings)
add_time = time.time() - t_add
print(f"✅ Added {ivf_index.ntotal:,} vectors in {add_time:.2f}s")

# ── Search with different nprobe values ───────────────────────────────
query = "breakthrough in artificial intelligence research"
q_vec = model.encode([query], normalize_embeddings=True).astype(np.float32)

print(f"\n🔍 Query: '{query}'")
print("=" * 65)
print(f"\n📊 nprobe SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS:")
print(f"  {'nprobe':<10} {'Time(ms)':<12} {'Top Result Score':<20}")
print(f"  {'─'*10} {'─'*12} {'─'*20}")

for nprobe in [1, 5, 10, 50, nlist]:
    ivf_index.nprobe = nprobe
    t = time.time()
    distances, indices = ivf_index.search(q_vec, k=3)
    query_ms = (time.time() - t) * 1000
    top_score = distances[0][0]
    print(f"  {nprobe:<10} {query_ms:.2f}ms{'':<6} {top_score:.4f}")

# Final results with optimal nprobe
ivf_index.nprobe = 20
distances, indices = ivf_index.search(q_vec, k=5)

print(f"\n📌 Top-5 Results (nprobe=20):")
for rank, (dist, idx) in enumerate(zip(distances[0], indices[0])):
    print(f"  Rank {rank+1}: {documents[idx][:70]}")
    print(f"           Score: {dist:.4f}")
```

sections.title: CODE EXAMPLE 2 — IVF-PQ (IVF + Product Quantization) — Memory Efficient
sections.body:
```python
# pip install faiss-cpu==1.9.0 sentence-transformers==3.4.0 numpy==2.2.0

import faiss
import numpy as np
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer

model = SentenceTransformer("sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2")

# ── Legal document search ─────────────────────────────────────────────
legal_docs = [
    "The defendant waives all rights under Section 15 of the Civil Code",
    "Intellectual property rights are protected under international law",
    "Contract breach occurs when one party fails to fulfill obligations",
    "The court ruled in favor of the plaintiff citing precedent cases",
    "Non-disclosure agreements protect confidential business information",
    "Arbitration provides an alternative dispute resolution mechanism",
    "Due diligence requires thorough examination before business transactions",
    "Fiduciary duty obligates trustees to act in beneficiary's best interest",
] * 10000  # 80,000 documents

print(f"📚 Legal corpus: {len(legal_docs):,} documents")

# Encode
embeddings = model.encode(
    legal_docs, batch_size=512, normalize_embeddings=True,
    show_progress_bar=True
).astype(np.float32)

dimension = embeddings.shape[1]  # 384
N = len(legal_docs)
nlist = int(np.sqrt(N))  # ~283

# ── Memory Comparison ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
flat_memory = N * dimension * 4 / (1024**2)  # MB
print(f"\n💾 Memory Analysis:")
print(f"   Flat Index:  {flat_memory:.1f} MB")

# IVF-PQ Configuration:
# m = number of sub-vectors (must divide dimension evenly)
# bits = bits per sub-vector (8 = 256 centroids per sub-vector)
m = 8      # 384 / 8 = 48 dimensions per sub-vector
bits = 8   # 2^8 = 256 centroids per sub-quantizer

pq_memory = N * m * bits / (8 * 1024**2)  # Approximate
print(f"   IVF-PQ Index: ~{pq_memory:.1f} MB (compressed!)")
print(f"   Compression ratio: ~{flat_memory/max(pq_memory,0.01):.0f}x")

# ── Build IVF-PQ Index ────────────────────────────────────────────────
quantizer = faiss.IndexFlatL2(dimension)
ivfpq_index = faiss.IndexIVFPQ(
    quantizer,
    dimension,
    nlist,  # clusters
    m,      # sub-vectors
    bits    # bits per sub-vector
)

print(f"\n🏋️  Training IVF-PQ (nlist={nlist}, m={m}, bits={bits})...")
ivfpq_index.train(embeddings)
ivfpq_index.add(embeddings)
print(f"✅ Index ready | {ivfpq_index.ntotal:,} vectors")

# Set search parameters
ivfpq_index.nprobe = 20

# ── Search ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
query = "intellectual property protection for software patents"
q_vec = model.encode([query], normalize_embeddings=True).astype(np.float32)

distances, indices = ivfpq_index.search(q_vec, k=5)

print(f"\n🔍 Query: '{query}'")
print("=" * 65)
unique_docs = list(dict.fromkeys([legal_docs[i] for i in indices[0]]))
for rank, doc in enumerate(unique_docs[:5]):
    print(f"\nRank {rank+1}: {doc}")

print("\n✅ IVF-PQ achieves ~95% recall with massive memory savings!")
```

sections.title: Concept Explanation
sections.body:
```
LSH = Hash similar vectors into the same BUCKET
      Similar items → same hash → search only that bucket

Core Idea: Unlike cryptographic hashes (SHA-256) which make 
           similar inputs look completely different, LSH makes 
           SIMILAR inputs hash to SAME value on purpose!

✅ Very fast — O(1) amortized query time
✅ Works well for binary/sparse vectors
✅ Low memory usage
❌ Lower accuracy than HNSW or IVF
❌ Tuning hash functions is complex
```

sections.title: Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
LSH — Random Projection Method:

Step 1: Create random hyperplanes
        Hyperplane 1: w1 = [0.3, -0.7, 0.5]
        Hyperplane 2: w2 = [-0.2, 0.8, 0.1]
        Hyperplane 3: w3 = [0.9, 0.1, -0.4]

Step 2: Hash each vector
        Vector A = [0.1, 0.9, 0.4]
        sign(A·w1) = sign(0.03-0.63+0.2) = sign(-0.4) = 0
        sign(A·w2) = sign(-0.02+0.72+0.04)= sign(0.74) = 1
        sign(A·w3) = sign(0.09+0.09-0.16) = sign(0.02) = 1
        Hash(A) = "011"  → Bucket "011"

        Vector B = [0.2, 0.8, 0.5] (similar to A!)
        Hash(B) = "011"  → Same Bucket "011" ✓

        Vector C = [0.9, 0.1, 0.1] (different!)
        Hash(C) = "100"  → Different Bucket "100" ✗

Query → Hash → Look in that bucket → Return matches

Buckets:
  "000" → [vec5, vec9]
  "001" → [vec3]
  "011" → [vecA, vecB] ← Query lands here!
  "100" → [vecC, vec7]
  "111" → [vec1, vec2, vec8]
```

sections.title: CODE EXAMPLE — LSH with FAISS
sections.body:
```python
# pip install faiss-cpu==1.9.0 sentence-transformers==3.4.0 numpy==2.2.0

import faiss
import numpy as np
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer

model = SentenceTransformer("sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2")

documents = [
    "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog",
    "Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence",
    "Python programming language is widely used for data science",
    "Deep learning requires large amounts of labeled training data",
    "Natural language processing helps computers understand human language",
    "Computer vision enables machines to interpret visual information",
    "Reinforcement learning trains models using reward and punishment",
    "Neural networks are inspired by the human brain structure",
] * 500  # 4000 docs

embeddings = model.encode(
    documents, batch_size=256, normalize_embeddings=False
).astype(np.float32)

dimension = embeddings.shape[1]

# ── LSH Index in FAISS ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# nbits = number of hash bits (higher = more buckets = less collision)
nbits = 512  # Should be multiple of 64, typically 2x-8x dimension

lsh_index = faiss.IndexLSH(dimension, nbits)
lsh_index.add(embeddings)

print(f"✅ LSH Index: {lsh_index.ntotal} vectors, {nbits} hash bits")

# Query
query = "How do neural networks process language?"
q_vec = model.encode([query]).astype(np.float32)

distances, indices = lsh_index.search(q_vec, k=5)

print(f"\n🔍 Query: '{query}'")
print("=" * 60)
unique = set()
for dist, idx in zip(distances[0], indices[0]):
    doc = documents[idx]
    if doc not in unique:
        unique.add(doc)
        print(f"  📄 {doc}")
        print(f"     Hamming Distance: {dist:.0f}")
```

sections.title: Concept Explanation
sections.body:
```
ANNOY (Approximate Nearest Neighbors Oh Yeah!) by Spotify
  = Build a FOREST of binary trees
  = Each tree splits data by random hyperplanes
  = Query traverses multiple trees, takes union of results

KD-TREE
  = Binary tree splitting on alternating dimensions
  = Works great for low dimensions (< 20D)
  = Poor for high-dimensional vectors (curse of dimensionality)

ANNOY Parameters:
  n_trees   = Number of trees (more = better accuracy, more memory)
  search_k  = Nodes to inspect at query time
```

sections.title: Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
ANNOY — Random Projection Tree:

Tree 1:              Tree 2:
      [root]               [root]
     /      \             /      \
  [A,B,C]  [D,E,F]    [A,D]   [B,C,E,F]
  /   \    /   \       |      /      \
[A,B][C] [D,E][F]     [A,D] [B,C]  [E,F]

Query Q:
  Tree 1: Q → goes RIGHT → [D,E,F] subtree → finds D,E,F
  Tree 2: Q → goes RIGHT → [B,C,E,F] → finds B,C,E,F

Union: {D, E, F, B, C}
Rescore → Return top-K

More trees = More candidates = Higher recall ✓
```

sections.title: CODE EXAMPLE — Annoy Index
sections.body:
```python
# pip install annoy==1.17.3 sentence-transformers==3.4.0 numpy==2.2.0

from annoy import AnnoyIndex
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
import time

model = SentenceTransformer("sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2")

# ── Recipe search use case ────────────────────────────────────────────
recipes = [
    "Spaghetti Carbonara: pasta with eggs, cheese, pancetta and black pepper",
    "Chicken Tikka Masala: spiced chicken in creamy tomato sauce",
    "Caesar Salad: romaine lettuce with Caesar dressing and croutons",
    "Beef Tacos: seasoned ground beef in corn tortillas with salsa",
    "Margherita Pizza: tomato sauce, mozzarella and fresh basil",
    "Pad Thai: stir-fried rice noodles with shrimp, peanuts and lime",
    "French Onion Soup: caramelized onions in beef broth with cheese crouton",
    "Sushi Roll: vinegared rice with fish and vegetables wrapped in seaweed",
    "Chocolate Lava Cake: warm chocolate cake with molten center",
    "Greek Salad: cucumbers, tomatoes, olives and feta cheese",
    "Butter Chicken: tender chicken in rich buttery tomato gravy",
    "Ramen: Japanese noodle soup with pork belly and soft-boiled egg",
]

# Generate embeddings
embeddings = model.encode(recipes, normalize_embeddings=True)
dimension = embeddings.shape[1]  # 384

# ── Build Annoy Index ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# metric: 'angular' (cosine), 'euclidean', 'manhattan', 'dot'
annoy_idx = AnnoyIndex(dimension, metric='angular')

for i, vec in enumerate(embeddings):
    annoy_idx.add_item(i, vec.tolist())

# n_trees: more trees = better accuracy, more build time
n_trees = 50
print(f"🔨 Building Annoy index with {n_trees} trees...")
t = time.time()
annoy_idx.build(n_trees)
build_time = time.time() - t
print(f"✅ Built in {build_time:.3f}s")

# Save index
annoy_idx.save('recipes.ann')
print("💾 Index saved to recipes.ann")

# ── Query ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def search_recipes(query_text, top_k=3, search_k=-1):
    """
    search_k: nodes to inspect. -1 = n_trees * top_k (auto)
              Higher search_k = more accurate but slower
    """
    q_vec = model.encode([query_text], normalize_embeddings=True)[0]
    indices, distances = annoy_idx.get_nns_by_vector(
        q_vec, top_k,
        search_k=search_k,  # -1 = automatic
        include_distances=True
    )
    return [(recipes[i], 1 - d) for i, d in zip(indices, distances)]

# Test queries
test_queries = [
    "vegetarian Italian pasta dish",
    "spicy Indian curry with chicken",
    "Japanese noodle bowl soup",
]

for query in test_queries:
    results = search_recipes(query, top_k=3)
    print(f"\n🔍 '{query}'")
    print("─" * 55)
    for rank, (recipe, score) in enumerate(results, 1):
        print(f"  {rank}. {recipe[:60]}")
        print(f"     Similarity: {score:.4f}")
```

sections.title: Concept Explanation
sections.body:
```
HYBRID = Dense Vector Search + Sparse Keyword Search (BM25/TF-IDF)

Why Hybrid?
  Dense Only:  Great for semantic meaning, bad for exact keywords
               Query "GPT-4" might miss documents with "GPT-4"
  Sparse Only: Great for exact keywords, bad for meaning
               "automobile" won't match "car"
  HYBRID:      Best of both worlds! ✓

Score = α × Dense_Score + (1-α) × Sparse_Score
         (Reciprocal Rank Fusion or Weighted Sum)

α = 0.7 means 70% semantic + 30% keyword
```

sections.title: CODE EXAMPLE — Hybrid RAG with BM25 + FAISS
sections.body:
```python
# pip install faiss-cpu==1.9.0 sentence-transformers==3.4.0
# pip install rank-bm25==0.2.2 numpy==2.2.0

import faiss
import numpy as np
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
from rank_bm25 import BM25Okapi
import re
from typing import List, Dict

model = SentenceTransformer("sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2")

# ── Medical knowledge base ─────────────────────────────────────────────
documents = [
    "Metformin is the first-line drug for treating Type 2 diabetes mellitus",
    "Insulin therapy is essential for Type 1 diabetes patients",
    "Hypertension management includes ACE inhibitors like Lisinopril",
    "Aspirin is used for cardiovascular disease prevention in high-risk patients",
    "Statins like Atorvastatin reduce LDL cholesterol and prevent heart disease",
    "Beta-blockers control heart rate and blood pressure in cardiac patients",
    "Antibiotics like Amoxicillin treat bacterial respiratory infections",
    "Ibuprofen and Paracetamol are common analgesics for pain management",
    "Chemotherapy drugs like Cisplatin are used in cancer treatment protocols",
    "Anticoagulants like Warfarin prevent blood clots in atrial fibrillation",
]

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# DENSE INDEX (FAISS)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
embeddings = model.encode(documents, normalize_embeddings=True).astype(np.float32)
dimension = embeddings.shape[1]

dense_index = faiss.IndexFlatIP(dimension)
dense_index.add(embeddings)

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# SPARSE INDEX (BM25)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def tokenize(text: str) -> List[str]:
    """Simple tokenizer for BM25"""
    return re.findall(r'\b\w+\b', text.lower())

tokenized_docs = [tokenize(doc) for doc in documents]
bm25 = BM25Okapi(tokenized_docs)

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# RECIPROCAL RANK FUSION (RRF)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def reciprocal_rank_fusion(
    dense_indices: List[int],
    sparse_indices: List[int],
    k: int = 60  # RRF constant
) -> List[tuple]:
    """
    RRF Score = Σ 1/(k + rank_i)
    Combines rankings from multiple retrieval systems
    """
    rrf_scores: Dict[int, float] = {}

    for rank, idx in enumerate(dense_indices):
        rrf_scores[idx] = rrf_scores.get(idx, 0) + 1 / (k + rank + 1)

    for rank, idx in enumerate(sparse_indices):
        rrf_scores[idx] = rrf_scores.get(idx, 0) + 1 / (k + rank + 1)

    # Sort by RRF score descending
    return sorted(rrf_scores.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# HYBRID SEARCH FUNCTION
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def hybrid_search(query: str, top_k: int = 5):
    print(f"\n🔍 Hybrid Search: '{query}'")
    print("=" * 65)

    # Dense retrieval
    q_vec = model.encode([query], normalize_embeddings=True).astype(np.float32)
    dense_dist, dense_idx = dense_index.search(q_vec, k=top_k * 2)
    dense_results = dense_idx[0].tolist()

    # Sparse retrieval (BM25)
    query_tokens = tokenize(query)
    bm25_scores = bm25.get_scores(query_tokens)
    sparse_results = np.argsort(bm25_scores)[::-1][:top_k * 2].tolist()

    # Show individual results
    print(f"\n📊 Dense Top-3:")
    for r in dense_results[:3]:
        print(f"   {documents[r][:65]}")

    print(f"\n📊 Sparse (BM25) Top-3:")
    for r in sparse_results[:3]:
        print(f"   {documents[r][:65]}")

    # Fuse results using RRF
    fused = reciprocal_rank_fusion(dense_results, sparse_results)

    print(f"\n🏆 HYBRID Results (RRF Fusion) Top-{top_k}:")
    print("─" * 65)
    for rank, (idx, score) in enumerate(fused[:top_k], 1):
        print(f"  {rank}. [{score:.4f}] {documents[idx]}")

# ── Test hybrid search ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
hybrid_search("diabetes medication treatment")
hybrid_search("heart disease prevention drugs")
hybrid_search("Metformin dosage for blood sugar")
```

When to use what:
  < 10K docs:    → FLAT (exact, simple, fast enough)

  Low memory:    → IVF-PQ (maximum compression)
  Read-only:     → Annoy (fast reads, no updates)
